subject: SKU duration caps, invoice routing and distributor netback for GCP private offer

Subject: SKU duration caps, invoice routing and distributor netback for GCP private offer

Aaron / Maya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow up on the private offer packaging we discussed: Cloud Retail AI is interested in a 24-month committed SKU but they want the ability to consume credits for sustained bursts without re-pricing mid-term. Two items we need to lock down before legal/procurement:

1) SKU duration cap vs. list-price anchoring: do we keep the SKU anchored to list price and apply a committed discount (credit bucket), or do we expose a "reservable bundle" SKU that traffics at a lower net price while still showing list price on the marketplace? The latter helps buyer perception but complicates distributor invoicing.

2) Distributor netback routing: Maya, you mentioned earlier that ResellerCo needs a 9–12% uplift to cover VAT handling and local invoice routing. Can you confirm whether ResellerCo requires list-price-based commissioning or a netback on actual billed tokens? That affects how we surface the private offer and whether we create an invoice pass-through.

I've attached a lightweight SKU-pack-pricing-model.xlsx with two sample approaches (list-anchored credit bucket vs. reservable bundle with holdbacks). Ben, looping you in for the margin workback — see the note in the model.

Goal: agree on approach by end of week so we can hand to Cloud Retail AI procurement (they want a procurement-ready summary by Apr 4).

Cheers,
Naomi

Subject: Re: SKU duration caps, invoice routing and distributor netback for GCP private offer

Naomi —

Thanks for the summary and the model. Quick answers from ResellerCo side:

• Reseller netback: we prefer a netback on actual billed tokens. List-price-based commissioning creates tax and reconciliation overhead for us in EMEA.
• Uplift: to make the economics neutral for ResellerCo (VAT, local remittance, invoice processing), we need a 10% uplift on top of the Redwood net. That can be modeled as a distributor holdback or as a pass-through fee on the invoice.
• Invoice path: we can accept either vendor-billed (Redwood invoices Cloud Retail AI and we receive a settlement) or reseller-billed (we invoice Cloud Retail AI directly) — reseller-billed is cleaner for us but procurement teams sometimes push back.

If you can model the netback as a simple % holdback in the spreadsheet that we can reconcile monthly, that would be ideal. I’ll try to put together the legal/invoicing constraints from our side by tomorrow.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Partnerships, ResellerCo
maya@resellerco.com

From: ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SKU duration caps, invoice routing and distributor netback for GCP private offer

Maya / team —

Appreciate the clear ask. I updated the attached netback_workback.csv and added a third packaging option in-line here to reduce reconciliation complexity:

Option A — List-anchored credits: SKU shows list price. Buyer consumes credits drawn from a committed bucket with a flat committed discount (easier for procurement). Distributor receives a monthly settlement as % of billed tokens (requires reconciliation).

Option B — Reservable bundle SKU: SKU is published at a lower bundle price on the marketplace (buyer sees lower price). We track an internal list-price for accounting; distributor uplift is modeled as a 10% gross adjustment applied to our net price at settlement (simpler distributor settlements, more complexity in marketplace UI).

Option C — Hybrid floor + pass-through: Publish SKU at list with a monthly usage floor and a pass-through invoice line for distributor fee (minimizes marketplace confusion and keeps legal procurement happy). Reconciliation is a simple monthly true-up.

My recommendation: go with Option C for Cloud Retail AI because their procurement team has asked specifically to see list price on the private offer (internal compliance) but they also want the distributor to be paid on actual billed usage. This gives us the cleanest procurement narrative and keeps ResellerCo's reconciliation down to one monthly true-up.

Timeline: if we agree today, I can (1) update the SKU-pack-pricing-model.xlsx with the C flow and (2) generate a one-page procurement summary for Cloud Retail AI.

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Deals, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: netback_workback.csv (CSV with worked examples)

1) Can Redwood include the monthly true-up calculation in the private offer documentation (we need an auditable line item for procurement)?
2) For the pass-through invoice line, will ResellerCo accept a consolidated monthly settlement or do they need per-region splits?
3) What’s the cutover timeline if we accept Option C? We need procurement-ready wording by Apr 4 to process with our GCP marketplace team.

If you can send a one-page procurement summary and a sample pass-through invoice (PDF) today, I can run it through our legal and circle back.
